Incremental Kolmogorov-Smirnov drift detector

Source: R/dfr_iks.R
dfr_iks.Rd

Unsupervised drift detection of dos Reis et al. (2016): for every monitored feature, a two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test between a reference sample and the sliding window of the last window_size observations, computed incrementally with iks(). A drift is signalled when the test rejects the null hypothesis for at least one feature. The detector monitors virtual concept drift (the feature distribution), without labels.

Usage

dfr_iks(
  target_feat = NULL,
  window_size = 100,
  alpha = 0.001,
  ca = iks_ca(alpha),
  reference = c("fixed", "consecutive"),
  tie_break = TRUE,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

target_feat

Features to be monitored (by default every numeric column).

window_size

Size W of the reference sample and of the sliding window.

alpha

Significance level of the test.

ca

Coefficient of the critical value ca sqrt(2 / W); by default iks_ca(alpha), 1.9495 for alpha = 0.001 (the paper and the reference code use the table value 1.95).

reference

"fixed" (the default, the paper's method): the reference sample is the first W observations (the data the model was trained on) and the window starts as a copy of it; after a drift the reference becomes the current window. "consecutive": the reference is the window of the W observations before the current window (the consecutive sliding windows of Zliobaite, 2010, the CD baseline of the paper).

tie_break

Pair every observation with a random value to break ties (TRUE, the default, as IKSSW of the reference code); otherwise the statistic can be overestimated when values repeat, in particular while the window overlaps the reference.

seed

Seed of the private generator of the sketches.

Value

dfr_iks object

Details

The output of each observation (drifter_output after fit()) has the statistic of every monitored feature (D_<feature>) and drift. After a drift with reference = "consecutive", both windows restart.

References

dos Reis, D. M., Flach, P., Matwin, S. and Batista, G. (2016). Fast unsupervised online drift detection using incremental Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. In Proceedings of the 22nd ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, 1545-1554. doi:10.1145/2939672.2939836

Zliobaite, I. (2010). Change with delayed labeling: when is it detectable? In 2010 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining Workshops, 843-850. doi:10.1109/ICDMW.2010.49

Examples

library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)
set.seed(1)
data <- data.frame(a = c(rnorm(600), rnorm(600, 1)), b = rnorm(1200))
detector <- fit(dfr_iks(window_size = 100, seed = 1), data)
which(detector$drifter_output$drift)
#> [1] 662
